## Verdict
- Answer: Ozempic news is steady and high-volume: 22,214 articles mentioning the term from June 2024 to May 2026 [c1]. About 68% are flagged critical [c1], yet overall polarity is close to the corpus norm (ratio 0.61 against a 0.58 baseline) [c1]. Coverage centres on GLP-1 and obesity, drug pricing and Novo Nordisk, and is dominated by the US.
- Decision: Treat Ozempic as a durable, mainstream, scrutiny-heavy topic. Plan for sustained critical coverage (safety, pricing, compounding) rather than a fading story. Do not read "critical" as "negative".
- Confidence: medium - the counts are complete for the window [c1], but the window ends 2026-05-31, about 145 days before today, and tone and critical flags are machine-assigned.
- What would change it: A post-May-2026 read showing a sustained shift in volume or critical share, or article-level checks showing the critical flag overstates real criticism.

## What the data shows
- Volume: 22,214 articles in the window 2024-06-01 to 2026-05-31, match mode "mention" [c1]. The critical flag covers 15,062 of them, or 67.8% [c1].
- Direction: the monthly series is flat to mildly rising. The late third totals 8,217 against 6,684 in the early third, a ratio of 1.23 (CAGR 11.9%) [c1]. The peak was March 2026 at 1,470 articles [c1].
- Tone: 37.9% negative, 61.8% positive [c1]. The negative-to-positive ratio is 0.61 against a corpus baseline of 0.58, 1.05 times baseline, "about as negative as ordinary news coverage" [c1].
- Themes (lift over corpus share) [c1]:
  - Tags: glp-1 (10,484 articles, lift 427.7), obesity (4,937, lift 383.9), fda (4,006), medicare (1,970).
  - Subcategories: diabetes medication management (3,315), drug pricing and reimbursement (2,323), compounding (717).
  - Taxonomy: Weight Loss (7,617) and Drugs & Medications (11,507).
- Organisations (machine-labelled, not verified) [c1]: Novo Nordisk 4,568 articles (20.5%), Lilly 940, Hims & Hers 399, Pfizer 468.
- People (machine-labelled, not verified) [c1]: "eli lilly" appears as a person label (2,247) and is likely a mislabelled company. Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has 628, and celebrities appear too: Lizzo 290, Rebel Wilson 146, Kelly Clarkson 130.
- Places: US 9,665 articles (40.8%), UK 2,581 (10.9%), Canada 1,086, India 1,049, Denmark 753 (lift 11.1) [c1]. Only 55.8% of articles were placed (11,873 of 21,260) [c1]. Place is where the article is about, not where it was published [c1].
- Source concentration: low. In a 197-article sample, the top publisher (yahoo.com) held 10.2% and the top three held 15.2%, across 134 distinct publishers [c1]. This is a sample of recent articles, not the full window [c1].
- Critical stories (the call returned only 3 of 8 requested; the rest were unresolved) [c1]:
  - 2026-03-09, braunschweiger-zeitung.de: Vitamin D deficiency risk with Ozempic and similar drugs. https://www.braunschweiger-zeitung.de/ratgeber-wissen/article411257613/abnehmen-ozempic-vitamin-d-omega-3-dr-riedl-warnt-vor-erhoehtem-sterberisiko.html
  - 2026-03-11, ibtimes.co.uk: Wegovy eye-complication warning, about 1 in 10,000 users, with a risk five times higher than on Ozempic. https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/experts-warn-1-10000-wegovy-users-face-5x-higher-risk-leading-serious-eye-complications-1784867
  - 2026-04-19, theweek.in: Op-ed on the global weight-loss revolution redefining obesity. https://www.theweek.in/columns/dr-preetha-peddy/2026/04/11/the-global-weight-loss-revolution-how-drugs-are-redefining-obesity.html

## Trend

The first month had 769 articles and the last 954 [c1]. The late-third to early-third ratio is 1.23, and the critical series is 1.17 [c1]. The tool labels the direction "flat" [c1].

## Comparison
Baseline: the corpus-wide negative-to-positive article ratio, 0.58 [c1].

| Measure | Ozempic | Baseline | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Neg/pos ratio | 0.61 [c1] | 0.58 [c1] | 1.05x [c1] |

Critical share ranged from 55.9% (July 2025) to 75.7% (July 2024) [c1]. There is no corpus baseline for the critical share, so it cannot be compared.

## Method and limits
- Window: 2024-06-01 to 2026-05-31, with the end date exclusive at 2026-06-01 [c1]. The gap to today (2026-10-23) is about 145 days, so nothing since May 2026 is covered.

## Method and limits

The article-count window ends **2026-05-31** [c1], with a **2026-06-01** [c1] censor cutoff; that is **144 days** before today, **2026-10-23** [est.]. The newest month is excluded because ingestion lags publication. The match mode is “mention” for counts and panels; the recent and critical feeds use “central” matching. Corpus table reachability passed its historical row floor [c1], but that is not proof of complete ingestion. The overview reports **22,214** matching articles [c1]; this is a count of matched articles, not unique readers, exposure, or drug use. Criticality and polarity are model labels. Sentiment uses one polarity per article; theme and entity labels can overlap. Geography and entity labels lag ingestion. The source concentration figures come from a recent sample, not the whole period. The data cannot establish causality, clinical risk, public opinion, or a full census of critical headlines.
